jia (Product Design): quick design check — bulk 'Remove access' flow for dashboard teams. attached mock in drive: https://go.mock/redwood/bulk-remove : thinking about validation + destructive confirmation UX. thoughts? :thinking_face: rohan (PM): prefer minimal friction. can we avoid typed confirm for >100 rows? feels heavy for ops. lex (Eng): typed confirm is simple to implement but worst for mobile. also increases support touches for typos. maya (Accessibility): if we keep typed confirm, we must make it keyboard-first and readable by screen readers. focus should go to the input and aria-live should announce success/failure. also ensure contrast on the danger CTA. sam (Design): option A: inline checkbox + big red CTA + small undo toast. Option B: typed confirm on >50 rows, with clear microcopy. I sketched both. rohan (PM): what's the metric tradeoff? more accidental deletes vs slower completes. can we measure? alexa (DevEx): we can A/B feature flag: control = current modal+undo; variant = typed confirm for bulk > N. track confirm rate, aborts, support tickets. lex (Eng): engineering concerns: typed confirm necessitates extra validation and error state handling. also mobile keyboard covers CTA, needs repositioning. maya (Accessibility): sample aria snippet — use aria-describedby to point to the validation message, and aria-invalid on the input. avoid using only color to convey error. example:```html
Must match "DELETE" exactly.
``` jia (Product Design): love that snippet. also thinking about required marker debate on the form that triggers this flow: should we keep a visible 'Required' label vs an asterisk with sr-only text? legal asked for explicit 'required' on some fields. sam (Design): my take — use asterisk for compact lists (teams table), but on longer forms use explicit 'Required' text. for the modal confirm, put a clear sentence: "This action will remove access for X users. Type DELETE to proceed." rohan (PM): can we soften copy and add progressive disclosure? like show impact summary first, then the typed confirm only if X > threshold. lex (Eng): progressive flow is fine. implement as stepper: step 1 impact summary (no typed), step 2 typed confirm for large batches. simpler to rollback. maya (Accessibility): ensure step changes are announced (aria-live region announcing "Step 2 of 2: Confirm"). do not rely on visual cues only. alexa (DevEx): rollout plan: feature-flag the stepper with typed confirm, enable telemetry: clicks on CTA, typed attempts, failures, time to confirm, device type. also add a kill switch. rohan (PM): agree. also add an undo retention window — 30s vs 5m? Ops prefers 5m. Thoughts? sam (Design): 30s feels short for large companies. recommend 5m by default, with an option for admins to set retention. surface undo toast with link to audit log. maria (pm — joins thread): @rohan also flagged that some customers require typed confirm for compliance. we should make it configurable per org. rohan (PM): ok make it configurable. lex (Eng): implementation notes: trap focus in modal, make confirm input the first tabbable element, disable primary CTA until exact match, and debounce paste to avoid accidental match. also ensure server-side double-check before executing destructive job. maya (Accessibility): last nit — don't auto-focus the confirm input if it causes mobile keyboard to push layout out of view. test on iOS with voiceover. provide a visible close button too. eng-bot: deploy-checklist: create feature flag, add telemetry events (bulk_remove_attempt, bulk_remove_confirmed, bulk_remove_cancelled, bulk_remove_undo), add admin setting for typed_confirm_required. jia (Product Design): next steps: sam to update mocks with stepper + microcopy, alexa to draft rollout/telemetry, lex to estimate effort, maya to run quick accessibility checklist. i'll schedule a 30m follow-up. :calendar: rohan (PM): thanks — sync in 48h. :thumbsup:
